source.version: Published ICCMETS 2026 conference proceedings paper; copyright 2026, printed pages 179–190 (12 PDF pages). The document has no dated version history; the citation record identifies the September 2026 proceedings version.

studies.label: Three-arm laboratory experiment: alternative solutions and campaign briefs

counts_source.locator: PDF p. 6 (printed p. 184), Table 1, caption and arm headings; PDF p. 4 (printed p. 182), Sections 3.1–3.2, randomized conditions and sample

arms.name: Unaided Control
arms.description: Creative problem-solving and ideation with no digital devices, search engines or AI interfaces (PDF p. 4, printed p. 182, Section 3.1).

arms.name: Unconstrained GenAI Access
arms.description: Unmonitored access to an LLM interface (GPT-4o / Claude 3.5 Sonnet), with free choice of how to use it (PDF p. 4, printed p. 182, Section 3.1).

arms.name: Structured Scaffolding
arms.description: Same LLM interface under the Cognitive Anchor-Rebound Protocol: at least three own ideas before opening the interface, critique and counter-factual prompts, and synthesis without copying AI text (PDF p. 4, printed p. 182, Section 3.1).

studies.task: Undergraduates proposed sustainable solutions to microplastic contamination in the Mekong Delta and wrote a 600-word campaign brief addressing rural education equity within one 90-minute session (PDF p. 5, printed p. 183, Section 3.3).

ai_tool.name: GPT-4o / Claude 3.5 Sonnet

estimates.notes: Table 1 reports participant composite scores with people per arm; unit and SD level are participant. The task-to-score mapping and aggregation across tasks are not fully described. The three-arm omnibus ANOVA is F(2, 477) = 165.23, p <.001, η² = .409. These are not pairwise statistics and are not entered in stats.test or stats.paper_effect. The paper does not print a total number of people specifically for this two-arm comparison; n_total is null. Section 4.1 names this outcome among the primary dependent variables, but no preregistration is stated. The p-value is the printed Tukey pairwise bound; no Tukey statistic, pairwise SE or confidence interval is printed. The paper labels the standardized effect d but does not define its standardizer. Unresolved source conflict: the Abstract instead reports d = −0.58, p < .001, for unconstrained access versus unaided control. stats.paper_effect retains d = −1.34 from Section 4.1, also repeated in Section 6; the abstract number is not silently corrected or treated as an independent contrast. Section 6 additionally prints "Conceptual Originality: -29.2% Drop (d = -1.34)"; its percentage calculation is not specified.

estimates.notes: Table 1 reports participant composite scores with people per arm; unit and SD level are participant. The task-to-score mapping and aggregation across tasks are not fully described. The three-arm omnibus ANOVA is F(2, 477) = 284.15, p <.001, η² = .543. These are not pairwise statistics and are not entered in stats.test or stats.paper_effect. The paper does not print a total number of people specifically for this two-arm comparison; n_total is null. Section 4.1 names this outcome among the primary dependent variables, but no preregistration is stated. Section 4.1 reports the Tukey pairwise bound p < .001, without a pairwise statistic or interval. Section 6 prints Fluency: +123% Increase, retained as an unstandardized paper effect without recomputation. The Abstract gives a conflicting three-arm fluency test: F(2,477) = 48.21, p < .001, η² = .168; Table 1 gives the omnibus values recorded above. Neither omnibus test is a two-arm effect.

not_extracted.what: Retrospective interviews and qualitative prompt-log archetypes
not_extracted.reason: PDF p. 5 (printed p. 183), Section 3.5, and PDF pp. 8–9 (printed pp. 186–187), Section 5: retrospective reports from 36 selected participants (12 per condition) and qualitative process accounts supply no eligible full-sample output-score contrast.

open_items: Fluency source conflict: Abstract (PDF p. 1, printed p. 179) prints F(2,477) = 48.21, p < .001, η² = .168; Table 1 (PDF p. 6, printed p. 184) prints F(2, 477) = 284.15, p < .001, η² = .543. The intended analysis is not established by the PDF.

Originality source conflict: unconstrained versus unaided d = −0.58 in the Abstract (PDF p. 1, printed p. 179), versus d = −1.34 in Section 4.1 and the Discussion box (PDF pp. 6, 9; printed pp. 184, 187). The body value is retained in stats and the abstract value is preserved in notes and its source quote; no arithmetic reconciliation was attempted.

The diversity analysis does not identify the observations, aggregation, SD basis, t-test subtype or standardized-effect denominator. Pairwise construction and t(318) do not establish participant-level uncertainty (PDF p. 5, printed p. 183, Section 3.4; PDF p. 7, printed p. 185, Section 4.2).

The task underlying each TTCT score and Table 2 metric, and any aggregation across the two tasks, are not specified; CAT scores are explicitly of the project briefs (PDF p. 5, printed p. 183, Section 3.4).

Exact random allocation, participant flow, attrition and exclusions are not described. Section 3.1 assigns arm counts to the randomized design and Table 1 reports matching analyzed counts; matching counts do not establish that no exclusions occurred (PDF pp. 4, 6; printed pp. 182, 184).

Which participants used GPT-4o versus Claude 3.5 Sonnet, how model choice was determined, and each tool’s release year are not specified. The stated 2024–2026 availability window is not an explicit release year; ai_tool.year remains null (PDF pp. 4, 11; printed pp. 182, 189).

The MANOVA dependent-variable list names four outcomes, whereas Table 1 contains six and omits Semantic Distance; the exact multivariate specification is unresolved (PDF p. 6, printed p. 184, Section 4.1).
The occupations and domain expertise of the two trained TTCT raters are unspecified, so elaboration cannot be assigned to lay/crowd or expert ratings (PDF p. 5, printed p. 183, Section 3.4).
The Discussion box’s percentage-change calculations, including Elaboration: +58% Increase, are not explained; values are transcribed without recomputation (PDF p. 9, printed p. 187, Section 6).

Pairwise SEs and confidence intervals are not printed, and many table-supported contrasts have no pairwise test or p-value. No two-arm sample total is printed for the extracted table contrasts; do not reuse the separate regression sample total as their n_total.
notes: Extraction B independently checked the complete 35,362-character markdown in three chunks and all 12 PDF pages with pymupdf; Tables 1–4 were recovered with find_tables. No research appendix, supplement or data/code link is identified. Table 4’s Appendix of Algorithmic Contribution is a proposed student deliverable, not a supplement. One randomized sample supplies all estimates; no shared-sample statement or preregistration is reported. Table 1 supplies six outcomes and three pairwise arm comparisons per outcome; Table 2 supplies cosine similarity and dispersion for the same three comparisons. Dispersion values are transcribed, not calculated. The proposed AI configuration is Structured Scaffolding and the default AI configuration is Unconstrained GenAI Access. All scored outputs were produced in the immediate session with assigned AI access available; no task after AI removal is reported. The three-arm univariate F tests and η² values are preserved in each outcome’s notes and Table 1 quotes, not misassigned as pairwise statistics. Section 4.1 also reports the combined-outcome three-arm MANOVA: Pillai’s Trace = 0.941, F(12,946) = 68.34, p < .001, partial η² = .470 (PDF p. 6, printed p. 184); this is not a two-arm outcome-specific effect. The reported relative changes in Section 6 are retained as percentages, not recomputed from table means. No exact numeric points are read from the ASCII originality-versus-fluency graphic (PDF p. 7, printed p. 185); its positions differ from Table 1 and may be schematic. The saved PDF ends with a truncated bibliography at printed p. 190. No arm sums, standardized effects, differences, uncertainty measures or sign reversals were computed. Numeric precision and signs are preserved in the verbatim source quotes, including trailing zeros not retained by JSON numeric formatting. Extraction completed 2026-10-11.
